annotation.title_clean: Robots and Labor Regulation: A Cross-Country/Cross-Industry Analysis
annotation.title_en: Robots and Labor Regulation: A Cross-Country/Cross-Industry Analysis
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Traverso, S.; Vatiero, M.; Zaninotto, E.
annotation.venue: DEM Working Papers, University of Trento (N. 2021/12)
annotation.summary_en: Working paper empirically examining how labor regulation, especially dismissal laws, relates to industrial robot adoption in nineteen Western countries from 2006 to 2016. Strict employment protection is negatively associated with robot adoption, but the effect is moderated by sectoral capital intensity, consistent with hold-up considerations.
key_provisions_or_claims: High statutory employment protection is negatively associated with industrial robot adoption.
Higher adjustment costs such as firing costs make robot investment riskier.
The correlation is positively mediated by sectoral capital intensity.
Firms may use robots to reduce worker bargaining power and hold-up opportunities.
The analysis covers 19 countries over 2006-2016 using IFR, EU KLEMS and Labor Regulation Index data.
